comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel analyze the performance of their Client/Client Computing segments (CCG) in relation to revenue drivers and operating outcomes. AMD reports that its Client segment operating income improved to a profit, primarily driven by higher revenue. Similarly, Intel analyzes its CCG segment, noting that revenue increased 4% primarily due to higher notebook volume, which was partially offset by lower desktop revenue and the exit of legacy businesses. While AMD highlights the net income flip to positive, Intel details the specific volume and mix shifts within the same product category.

sentences.text: Client operating income was $897 million in 2024, compared to operating loss of $46 million in 2023.
The increase in operating income was primarily due to higher revenue, partially offset by higher operating expenses.

CCG revenue increased 4% from 2023 primarily due to higher notebook volume compared to 2023 and was partially offset by lower other CCG revenue, which decreased from 2023 due to the exit of legacy businesses, and lower desktop revenue, which decreased on lower demand compared to 2023.
